# Installed host foundation consumers

## Purpose

Maintainer-owned regression evidence for agency through the ordinary installed
application client and portable FLOW artifact APIs. These consumers are authored
with platform context. They are not unfamiliar-consumer usability qualification.

## Ownership

- `materialize.ts` constructs three independent temporary consumer repositories and
  installs exact frozen Jig/FLOW archives using the installed-test conventions.
- `../private-profile-diagnostics.ts` owns bounded profile summaries shared with workspace review fixtures.
- Without a supplied FLOW archive, freeze the installed public SDK package.
  Never require a neighboring SDK source checkout.
- `adaptive/` owns deterministic candidate production, reviewed evaluation,
  independent acceptance, and explicit final artifact selection.
- `documents/` owns a separate noncoding producer/validator application.
- `evaluation-deadline/` owns separate generation and test timeout Runs through public operation errors.
- `recipe/` owns the exact TypeScript 5.7.3 and Zod 3.23.8 development closure.
  Its generated Bun lock is retained verbatim as `bun.lock.txt` and copied to the
  ordinary `bun.lock` filename when constructing a consumer.
- `../../host/installed-host-foundation.test.ts` owns native
  registration. Fixture modules register no tests and acquire no owners on import.

## Local Contracts

- Consumer methods import only public `@jigging/flow`. Application drivers import
  only public `@jigging/jig/client` plus ordinary platform libraries. Inert project
  declarations use the ordinary public Jig authoring entrypoint.
- Each separate application installs frozen archives normally. Its nested Jig
  project consumes the byte-identical SDK archive as a declared source workspace
  member. This qualifies source-workspace consumption of a frozen public artifact,
  not registry publication or standalone packaged-dependency consumption.
  `lockFoundationWorkspace` runs the pinned Bun's ordinary lock-only install before review, within the existing 120-second authoring allowance.
  It removes generated installation links, leaving review to prepare captured dependencies through the real native boundary.
  Review receives no resolution permission and must preserve the authored lock bytes.
- No private helpers, custom launchers, provider calls, source admission changes,
  runtime installation, or checkpoint assumptions enter these applications.
- Native opt-in and actual native prerequisite observation precede payloads.
  Missing prerequisites fail the whole selected host file. There are no skips.
- Preserve failed consumers, exact archive digests, and bounded private command
  transcripts. Delete successful temporary roots only after terminal cleanup and
  exported-byte assertions. Command exit alone is not cleanup evidence.
- Driver failures report fixed application stages and public client or terminal
  error codes. Preserve the original exception and exclude tickets, receipts,
  inputs, diagnostic payloads, and private state from this summary.
  Result-trace summaries reproject at most fourteen fixed result-phase start/end
  records with bounded timings and closed outcomes. Never forward raw trace
  lines, header identities, paths, arbitrary fields or exception payloads.
- Ordinary review commands enable the existing private profile in their own evidence directory.
  Failure summaries project at most forty existing phase events or normalized closed failure records, with closed capture status.
  Read at most 256 KiB and 1026 records. Retain the final events when projection truncates.
  Trace observation never replaces command failure.

  Evaluation review includes operand capture, preparation, normalization and disposal.
  Its nested dependency phase observes only actual preparation.
- Decode failure records through `normalizePrivateProfileFailure` before filtering timing phases.
  Failure records share the event limit and retain only fixed phases, closed causes and bounded times.
  Malformed failure records produce the existing invalid-summary status without forwarding arbitrary fields.
- The adaptive driver's joined Run may enable the existing private phase trace.
  Only its Run client receives that environment. Observation and export clients remain unprofiled.
  The fixture selector stays out of every installed command's environment.
  Run failure summaries reuse the review trace's input, record and event bounds.

  Project only existing host, containment, execution and settlement phases.
  Keep both candidate cycles within one finite 180-second root Run.
  Its allowance covers two 60-second evaluations and 60 seconds for producers, independent checking, and orchestration.
  Keep the existing 75-second client transport margin and all evaluation phase limits.
  Phase ceilings do not establish measured payload time or the deadline's underlying cause.
  Existing aggregate spans do not isolate every evaluator substep.
- Exact repeated exports reconcile their original delivery. Collision checks use
  a different selection at an existing destination and verify unchanged bytes.
- Candidate tests are process evidence, not independent acceptance. Deterministic
  iteration proves artifact/evaluation composition, not adaptation quality.
- Deadline controls retain bounded phase evidence through public `OperationError.details`.
  Each control receives a fresh Run and preserves ordinary evaluator limits.
  Stopped-phase snapshots require actual collection. Unavailable snapshots retain process evidence and an explicit null file manifest.
  Repeated public result reads must preserve the original evidence and cleanup.
- Cancellation and client-death cases await a real reviewed HTTP request.
  They then stop the original attempt and require settlement without replay.
  Request counts, protected owner rows and native residue provide independent
  observations. Prior completed results remain immutable.
- Before/after native residue compares this sequential profile's delegated
  `jig-run-` cgroups or acquired Linux user scopes, including their cgroups.
  Mac observation compares `org.jig.native.` launchd jobs.
  Installed Linux consumers without inherited delegation observe support first.
  Their public CLI must acquire the actual execution scope.
  Run no concurrent native owners in that qualification namespace during observation.

## Work Guidance

- Keep each application independent of the repository layout.
- Parent automation owns suite registration and frozen-profile reruns.

## Verification

- `bun packages/jig/test/fixtures/host-foundation/validate.ts` checks construction
  and bundles every owned consumer source without executing it.
- `bun test packages/jig/test/host/installed-host-foundation.test.ts` requires the
  exact qualified native profile and frozen archives (or already built packable
  candidates). Source validation does not substitute for this installed gate.
